origin: John P. Kotter, Harvard Business School, 1996
description: Sequential leadership model for driving large-scale organisational change. Emphasises urgency, coalition and short-term wins before institutionalising new ways of working.
best_for: Designing the change-management plan of a transformation roadmap
Sequencing quick wins versus structural change

steps.name: Create a sense of urgency
steps.description: Make the business case for change visible and undeniable to the leadership team.

steps.name: Build a guiding coalition
steps.description: Assemble a cross-functional group with the power, expertise and credibility to lead.

steps.name: Form a strategic vision and initiatives
steps.description: Clarify how the future differs from the past and which initiatives get there.

steps.name: Enlist a volunteer army
steps.description: Communicate the vision so that large numbers of people want to act on it.

steps.name: Enable action by removing barriers
steps.description: Remove structural, process and incentive obstacles that block change.

steps.name: Generate short-term wins
steps.description: Plan and deliver visible improvements within 6–12 months.

steps.name: Sustain acceleration
steps.description: Use credibility from early wins to tackle bigger, harder changes.

steps.name: Institute change
steps.description: Anchor new behaviours in culture, governance and performance management.

pitfalls: Declaring victory after the first quick win
Treating communication as a single announcement instead of a sustained campaign
A coalition made of the sponsor's direct reports only
